Hi,
Use a Standard RS485 adapter with A & B.  No ground need.

Don’t use a TTL 3.3V adapter directly.

Here an example of Adapter that works :
https://www.amazon.com/dp/B081MB6PN2 [tracking params removed]

On Mon, Jan 15, 2024, 11:14 a.m. Volthium Support <[vendor support email]> wrote:
Hello [Owner],

There are two options for battery reading, either RS485 or CAN if you purchase the Communication Hub. If you want to communicate in CAN, here's what we recommend:

  *   Communication Hub - 105$: https://volthium.com/fr/product/communication-hub-victron-ve-can/
  *   Victron Cerbo-S GX - 299.98$
  *   Victron GX Touch - 294.98$

If you wish to communicate via RS485, we can send you two XLR to RJ45 female cables to be able to communicate with your batteries. See the attached photos of the equipment that will be sent.

  *   XLR to RJ45 female - $10/Ea

Here are the pin details:

  *   Pin 7 RS485 A
  *   Pin 8 RS485 B

In addition, we will provide you with the RS485 protocol. Then, when you connect the XLR cable, you'll need to use the one closest to the negative terminal.

Does this answer all your questions?

Thank you,

[Support Agent]
[vendor support phone]

À: [vendor support email]
Objet: Voltage monitoring

Hello,

I am running 2 of your 12 V 200 Ah batteries (the version with built in heater and bluetooth, 12.8-200-G4DY-CH20 I think) in series at my off-grid cabin. One of the pain points for us is the hassle of knowing the battery charge level. The current process involves going upstairs with a mobile phone and using the app to connect over bluetooth to each battery and note which one is lower.

There are a couple of reasons why this is undesirable. One is that we encourage people to put their phones away at the cabin and the requirement to use an app is not convenient. Another is that the workflow of using the app is not easy for my in-laws to do. They are not particularly tech savvy.

My preferred solution is to install a small display in the kitchen that shows the overall percentage. I think it would be sensible to pull the state of charge information off the batteries using the data port on their side using a simple computer like an arduino. I am an electrical engineer (I design helicopter accessories) and I've done a small amount of work with canbus. Before I jump in, I have a few questions.

- Is the data port on the batteries CANBUS?
- Do you have any issues with this approach?
- Are you familiar with other customers doing anything comparable?
- Is there any guidance or suggestion you have for me as I start down this road?

Cheers,
  [Owner]
  Vancouver, BC
